h1: How does Newton zoning define and measure a half-story?
title: Newton Half-Story Definition: Ceiling Height and Floor Area
description: Learn the exact ceiling-height and floor-area test used in Newton's zoning definition of a half-story.
short_answer: Newton defines a half-story as a story directly under a sloping roof where the area with a ceiling height of at least 7 feet is less than two-thirds of the area of the story below. This zoning definition should be applied to the actual floor plan and roof geometry.

facts.text: Newton's definition uses a ceiling-height threshold of 7 feet and compares the qualifying area with the area of the story directly below.
A dormer or attic conversion should be checked against the half-story definition as well as the property's separate height and floor-area limits.

qa.q: Is a ceiling height of exactly 7 feet included in the calculation?
qa.a: Yes. Newton's definition uses an area with a ceiling height of 7 feet or greater.

items: The measured floor area with a ceiling height of 7 feet or greater
The area of the story directly below
